Survival sub-model that borrows a long-term tail from an external cohort

Source: R/survivalSubExternal.R
survivalSubExternal.Rd

Experimental. Predicting beyond the last follow-up of the study needs the baseline hazard there, which survivalSub() can only extrapolate (linearly in the cumulative hazard). When an external cohort with longer follow-up is available – an earlier generation of the same device, a registry, an older trial – its baseline hazard can supply the shape of the tail. survivalSubExternal() fits one Cox model to both cohorts with a generation indicator (1 for the study, 0 for the external cohort): $$h(t \mid x, g) = h_0(t) \exp(\beta^\top x + \gamma g),$$ so the study's hazard beyond its own follow-up is the external one scaled by \(e^\gamma\). Only the survival sub-model uses the external cohort; the longitudinal sub-model is fit on the study as usual, and the external cohort needs no biomarkers.

The key assumption is proportional hazards between the cohorts, also beyond the study's follow-up, where it cannot be checked. Within the overlap it is tested with cox.zph (stored in $external$ph_test, with a warning when \(p < 0.05\)); the test has little power with short study follow-up, so a non-significant result is weak reassurance, and a sensitivity analysis on the tail is advisable. The hazard ratio itself, estimated from the overlap only, can be noisy when the study is short and has few events, and the proportional hazards assumption carries that noise to the whole tail. tail_hr fixes it instead (the other coefficients are then re-estimated given it), for a sensitivity analysis over plausible values, e.g. c(0.8, 1, 1.25), or to use prior knowledge, e.g. that the generations are equivalent.

With splice = TRUE (the default) the external cohort only supplies the tail: up to the study's last follow-up \(\tau\) the baseline cumulative hazard is the Breslow estimate from the study alone (at the coefficients of the joint fit), and beyond \(\tau\) it continues with the increments of the joint fit's baseline, i.e. the external shape scaled by \(e^\gamma\). Within the study's follow-up predictions then rest on the study's own events. With splice = FALSE the joint fit's baseline is used throughout, so the external cohort (scaled by \(e^\gamma\)) also shapes the study's hazard within its follow-up, which matters when the cohorts are not proportional there.

Predictions are for the study population: when the prediction data have no generation column it is taken as 1.

Usage

survivalSubExternal(
  data_internal,
  data_external,
  form_marginal_surv,
  form_conditional_cr = NULL,
  generation = "generation",
  tail_hr = NULL,
  splice = TRUE
)

Arguments

data_internal, data_external

One row per subject, for the study and for the external cohort. Both need the variables of form_marginal_surv (and of form_conditional_cr, if given).

form_marginal_surv, form_conditional_cr

As in survivalSub, without the generation term, which is added.

generation

Name of the generation indicator column to create (it must not already exist).

tail_hr

NULL (default) to estimate the hazard ratio of the study against the external cohort, or a positive number to fix it.

splice

If TRUE (default), use the study's own baseline up to its last follow-up and the external shape only beyond it (see Details). Not available for a stratified Cox model.

Value

A survivalSub.BJM fit, usable wherever survivalSub()'s is (e.g. predictRisk(), fitImputedBJM(survival_fit_all = )), with an external element: the generation variable, the cohort sizes and follow-up, the hazard ratio of the study against the external cohort (hazard_ratio, the one used; hazard_ratio_estimated, from the data; tail_hr_fixed) and the PH test.

Examples

# \donttest{
data(pbc3)
surv <- pbc3[!duplicated(pbc3$id), ]
# pretend the study had 4 years of follow-up and the rest of pbc3 is external
id <- as.numeric(as.character(surv$id))
study <- surv[id %% 2 == 0, ]
study$status3[study$years > 4] <- 0
study$years <- pmin(study$years, 4)
external <- surv[id %% 2 == 1, ]
fit <- survivalSubExternal(study, external, Surv(years, status3) ~ age + sex, NULL)
fit$external
